reader.decision: Change only `report-builder` now: stop filtering archived invoices in monthly reports, or warn when the count is 0 but the tenant has invoices in the period. Hold the corrective migration until a snapshot is identified.
reader.decision_reason: The message says a restore is unsafe without a backup, snapshot or updated_at evidence, and it doesn't say any of these exists. The report-side change has no data risk and fixes the empty report.

reconstruction.problem: The October report for northwind came back empty. Migration 0042 archived all 188 of northwind's October invoices, although its README says it should archive only invoices older than 90 days. The report job most likely had `hide_archived` on for northwind, so it filtered out every archived invoice. The flag value itself is inferred from the counts and not verified.
reconstruction.what_breaks: northwind's monthly report is empty, and the job still logs report=ok because an empty result is not treated as an error. acme and globex also lost data to the migration (301 of 412 and 64 of 97 invoices archived), but their reports still show those invoices because their filter was off.
reconstruction.fix: Two options. (a) A corrective migration that restores the wrongly archived invoices. Aelita prefers this first, because the migration is the root cause. (b) A change to report-builder only: stop filtering archived invoices in monthly reports, or warn when the count is 0 but the tenant has invoices. (b) becomes primary if no snapshot exists.
reconstruction.cost: (a) needs a backup, snapshot or updated_at evidence that has not been located. Without one, a restore could un-archive invoices that were archived on purpose. (b) is a one-line change with no data risk, but it leaves the wrongly archived data in place.

follow_up_questions: Does a pre-migration snapshot or backup of the invoices table exist, or do updated_at values show which rows 0042 changed?
